                Concise Justification: Behavioral biases lead to initial underreaction to information (short-term momentum) followed by subsequent overreaction correction (long-term mean-reversion); a cross-sectional factor leveraging both horizons can identify mispricing.
                Concise Knowledge: If short-term returns (e.g., 5-day) exhibit momentum while long-term returns (e.g., 20-day) exhibit mean-reversion, then a composite signal subtracting long-term from short-term return captures both effects; when the composite is positive, it suggests ongoing momentum not yet overextended, while a negative composite indicates potential reversal.
                concise Specification: Factor = (close / close.shift(5) - 1) - (close / close.shift(20) - 1) / (20-day rolling standard deviation of daily returns); computed daily per stock using closing prices; requires at least 20 days of history.
